You will hear a teacher giving her class some information about a trip to a museum.

OK everyone, I'd like to tell you a bit about our class trip to the Natural History Museum tomorrow. We need to leave a little earlier than our usual school start time of 830, so please make sure you're ready and waiting at the school gate by 8, ready to set off at 8:15. There are loads of interesting things to see at the museum.
Our visit will focus on the Arctic region of the world, in particular the sea creatures there.

There are land animals too, but because we're studying the oceans in class at the moment, we'll concentrate on that. You'll have a great time looking at all the displays, but there's work to do too. Not a quiz this time. I'd like you to read the display information carefully and choose the most interesting item to make a drawing of. I know you'd probably like to take a photo or two, but no mobile phones.

So about lunchtime. The museum has a cafe, but the school kitchen will provide a packed lunch for everyone, including sandwiches, fruit and water. There's a lovely garden to walk around in beside the museum. The weather forecast is good for tomorrow, so we'll go down to the lake and have our picnic there.
We'll see more of the museum in the afternoon. Make notes because after our visit.

I'm going to ask you to write a report about it. Don't worry, you won't have to do a presentation you'll be pleased to hear. Before we go, I'd like you to look at some research by a famous professor, Helen Hawthorpe. I'll just spell her surname for you and you can look her up on the Internet. It's Haw.
Thorpe.
Any questions?
